task.description: Type D or E inline design for ISS-0669. The fix should: (1) Add an explicit Mutex around Pool.acquire() when called from raw OS threads (so only one thread calls the Io.Threaded completion-queuing at a time), OR (2) Document in Pool's API that callers MUST NOT call Pool.acquire() concurrently from raw std.Thread.spawn threads. If the investigation shows Io.Threaded is fundamentally not safe under raw-thread reentrancy, document this clearly. Also specify updates to tests/specs/ORD-01.md and tests/specs/ORD-04.md to document the constraint and the workaround.

result.summary: Design for ISS-0669 Pool mutex fix (src/db/pool.zig) — Type E prose artefact produced
changes_specified: Change 1: Pool struct field mutex: std.Io.Mutex -> std.Thread.Mutex
Change 2: Pool.init() .mutex = .init unchanged (compatible with both types)
Change 3: All lockUncancelable(self.io) -> lock(), all unlock(self.io) -> unlock() — 6 call sites in acquire() and release()
Change 4: acquire() — remove defer unlock at top; add explicit unlock after stale-conn block; add re-lock-pushback-unlock in error paths of maybeRedirectToTenantHost and applyRequestStorageRouting
Change 5: release() — SQL already outside lock; only signature changes needed

issues.description: stale-conn pg.Conn.connectUrl runs under lock — serialises acquire during reconnect; acceptable for correctness fix; out of scope
Conn._io Clock.real.now(io) still uses Io.Threaded from raw thread — affects only timestamping, not row-lock isolation; out of scope
